solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pop a question, somewhat unclear

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'Pop a question' are used, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: Someone asks a question that turns out to be rather vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop a question' suggests a proposal of marriage; it is just the text that hides the answer, and 'somewhat' shows only part is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque writing or thinking is hard to see through, so unclear.

clue.text: Risk connected with entering border from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the bottom, so the letters run upward
to enter is to go into something

parts.note: a lip is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A danger linked to crossing a frontier from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border from the south' sounds like a frontier crossing, but in a down entry the south is the bottom, so the letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: peril is danger or risk.

clue.text: After two pints, spot rear of venue for hard rock

parts.note: a zit is a spot on the skin

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Two pints in, someone spots the back of a venue that plays hard rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard rock' reads as the music, fitting pints and a venue; it is a literal hard rock. The puzzle has a rock-music theme running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartzite is a very hard metamorphic rock formed from sandstone.

clue.text: Clip from One Direction for spring festival

indicators.note: to clip from something is to trim it, here cutting off the final letter

parts.note: eastern is one direction, as in the eastern side

explanation.surface: A video snippet from the boy band One Direction marks a spring holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One Direction' looks like the band; it is EASTERN, which loses its last letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the Resurrection falls in spring each year.

clue.text: Referencing, in report, something from The Observer?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A newspaper item citing a story from The Observer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which fits 'report' and 'referencing'; here it is anyone who observes, and a sighting is what they come up with.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer's product is a sighting, something seen; the question mark flags the newspaper pun.

clue.text: Single women afflicted with heatstroke

indicators.note: afflicted letters are troubled and disordered, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unmarried women suffering in a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like it describes the women; it is the definition, a record released as a single. Smoke on the Water is the Deep Purple hard-rock hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke on the Water was released as a single by Deep Purple in 1973.

clue.text: Get stuck in dress worn by Dorothy's companion

parts.note: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A dress that gets snagged on Dorothy's little dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuck in' suggests being snagged or trapped, but it means doing something with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom match: both phrases mean throwing yourself into something with enthusiasm and no restraint.

clue.text: What may go with nail — biter?

definitions.meaning: the partner of 'nail' in a set phrase for fighting fiercely
a part of the mouth that does the biting

explanation.surface: A nail-biter, split by a dash into a question.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash breaks 'nail-biter' in two: one half is the phrase 'tooth and nail', the other a thing that bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooth pairs with nail in 'tooth and nail', and a tooth is literally a biter.

clue.text: Close call when new channel ultimately rejected by terrestrial

indicators.note: rejected by means the letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: an earthling is a terrestrial, an inhabitant of Earth

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, the last letter

explanation.surface: A near miss when a new TV channel is turned down by a terrestrial broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrestrial' suggests TV broadcasting, but here it is a noun for a being from Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, an outcome that nearly went the other way.

clue.text: Burns possibly to the ear? Blimey!

indicators.note: what reaches the ear is the sound, not the spelling

parts.note: Robert Burns, the national poet, is a great Scot

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on hearing about burns, perhaps from a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' capitalised at the start of the clue could be injuries; it is Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Scott! and Blimey! are both exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Staff follows how oenophile opens Muscat here

indicators.note: the staff word follows the opening letter in the answer
how the word opens points to the manner of its start, its opening letter
how a word opens is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wine lover uncorks a bottle of Muscat while staff look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscat' looks like the grape; it is the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of this Gulf sultanate, so it is located there.

clue.text: Sound of locksmith initially cutting key at this location

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the key word, sitting inside it

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: A locksmith cuts a key on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is the definition, as in sound of mind, not a noise; the key is the one on a computer keyboard, not a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone all there is mentally alert and sane, i.e. of sound mind.

clue.text: Island nation's leader moving right on time

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the pieces sit together
the first letter of the nation word shifts one place to the right, rearranging it

explanation.surface: An island nation's head of state swings rightwards in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island nation' reads as one phrase, but 'Island' alone is the definition and the nation is the Caribbean one whose first letter shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Charge one vehicle with meter

parts.note: a charge levied by the government

explanation.surface: A fee levied on a single vehicle fitted with a meter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' fits the fare on a meter, which is part of the definition's picture; here it is a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car whose fare is shown on a meter.

clue.text: Vegetable — with skill I bottle it

parts.note: to bottle it is to lose your nerve, to choke

explanation.surface: A cook confesses that, for all their skill, they make a mess of preserving vegetables in jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle it' suggests preserving vegetables in jars; it is British slang for losing your nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: The artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Former colony is the latest source of irritation

parts.note: the news is the latest information

explanation.surface: A complaint that a former colony is the newest thing to cause annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious split is NEW and a country, but the wordplay divides after the S, so the country is never clued directly.
explanation.definitionFit: New Spain was the Spanish colonial viceroyalty centred on Mexico.

clue.text: Wine mixed in iron pot

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Wine being stirred together in an iron cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like the link between wine and pot; it is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the red Burgundy grape gives its name to the wine made from it.

clue.text: Fights off policeman after losing head in present location?

indicators.note: after means this piece comes later in the answer
off means wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged
losing head means the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A policeman fends off fighters after a head injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' reads as here and now, but it is a gift, so the location is where gifts are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift shop is where presents are bought, so it is a location for presents, the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: The spies go flying rather high

indicators.note: letters sent flying land in a new order

explanation.surface: Spies taking to the air at a fair altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather high' seems to say how high the spies fly; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Steepish means somewhat steep, fairly high, as of a price or slope.

clue.text: Board member undressed nearby

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer layer, losing the first and last letters

parts.note: a knight is a piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A company director is caught without clothes close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board member' suggests a company director; it is a chess piece, KNIGHT, stripped of K and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old-fashioned word for near or close by.

clue.text: Dated northern town losing last plant in the end

indicators.note: losing last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Oldham is a town in Greater Manchester in northern England

indicators.note: in the end means take the final letter

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned northern town finally loses its last factory.
explanation.walkthrough: OLDHAM drops its last letter M, then T, the end of 'plant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old hat is out of fashion, stale and old-fashioned.

clue.text: Exonerate half of rock band then leave

indicators.note: half of means only the front half of the band's name is used

parts.note: AC/DC is the Australian hard-rock band

explanation.surface: A judge clearing half of a rock group, who then walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit is to clear someone of a charge, freeing them from blame.

clue.text: Overturn winning goal

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, winning
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A late winning goal turns a match on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' suggests football; it is an end in the sense of an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, to overturn it.

clue.text: Having lots of money is boring at the beginning, outstanding at the end

parts.note: a well is made by boring into the ground
work still outstanding is still to do

explanation.surface: Being rich is dull at first but excellent in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' and 'outstanding' read as dull and excellent; they mean drilling and not yet done. 'At the beginning' and 'at the end' only place the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means wealthy, having plenty of money.

clue.text: House in Russia — yes, in Russia — man left unfinished

indicators.note: 'left unfinished' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A Russian saying yes, and a man walking out before the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'in Russia' belongs once to the definition and once to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or cottage.

clue.text: Jack trimmed roses? No way man!

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: trimmed means both ends of roses are cut off, as when pruning

parts.note: the word whose inner letters are kept

explanation.surface: A gardener named Jack pruning roses, and someone protesting at the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the rhyming put-down 'No way, Jose!'; Jose is a Spanish man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase pairs a refusal with the name, so the man addressed in that phrase is called Jose.

clue.text: Mix stew outside one church then another

indicators.note: then means next in sequence, so the second church comes after the rest
the stew word goes outside the first church abbreviation

parts.note: a hotpot is a meat and potato stew, as in Lancashire hotpot
CH is the standard abbreviation for church
another church gives a second CH

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a stew outside one church, then moves on to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' looks like an instruction to rearrange, but it is the definition. A hotpot is a British layered stew of meat and sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is a confused jumble, a mixture of disparate things.

clue.text: Mineral, one extracted from meadow, placed by box

indicators.note: placed by means the word for box is set right beside the shortened meadow
extracted from means the letter for one is taken out of the word for meadow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to spar is to box, as boxers do in practice

explanation.surface: Something mined from a meadow and set down beside a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container but is the verb for fighting with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Feldspar is a common rock-forming silicate group found in granite, so it is a mineral.

clue.text: Sailor meets endlessly eccentric swinger in the woods

indicators.note: 'endlessly' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A sailor runs into an oddball swinging through the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' hints at a party-goer; it is Tarzan swinging on jungle vines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, the jungle hero, swings from tree to tree on vines.
